sentences.en: Since the mid-1970s, almost every jazz musician has owned a copy of the same book.
sentences.zh: 自20世纪70年代中期以来，几乎每位爵士乐手都拥有一本同样的书。

sentences.en: It has a peach-colored cover, a chunky 70s-style logo, and black plastic binding.
sentences.zh: 它有着桃色的封面、粗犷的70年代风格标志，以及黑色的塑料装订。

sentences.en: It is delightfully homemade-looking, like it was printed by a bunch of teenagers at Kinko's.
sentences.zh: 它看起来有一种令人愉悦的自制感，就像是一群青少年在金考快印店里印出来的一样。

sentences.en: And inside is the sheet music for hundreds of common jazz tunes, also known as jazz standards,
sentences.zh: 书里收录了数百首常见爵士乐曲的乐谱，也就是所谓的“爵士标准曲”，
全部都是用手写精心标注的。
它被称为《真实之书》（The Real Book）。

sentences.en: When I started playing jazz, I remember the first thing my guitar teacher said was,
sentences.zh: 我刚开始学爵士乐时，记得我的吉他老师说的第一句话就是：

sentences.en: well, you gotta buy a real book.

sentences.zh: 这是制作人米克尔·麦卡维农。

sentences.en: It just felt like something you were expected to own if you were a serious musician.
sentences.zh: 如果你想成为一名认真的音乐人，这似乎是你理应拥有的东西。

sentences.en: My high school jazz teacher, Mr. Leonard, had stacks of real books on his desk,
sentences.zh: 我的高中爵士乐老师伦纳德先生，他的桌子上堆满了《真实之书》，

sentences.en: and he told me that he actually got his first real book at the place where they were originally published,
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，他最初是在这本书的诞生地买到他的第一本《真实之书》的，

sentences.en: Berklee College of Music in Boston.
sentences.zh: 那就是波士顿的伯克利音乐学院。

sentences.en: He had just arrived for his freshman year.
sentences.zh: 那时他刚入学，还是个大一新生。

sentences.en: I heard people talking about the real book, the real book.
sentences.zh: 我听到人们在谈论《真实之书》，《真实之书》。

sentences.en: It was just all around Berklee.
sentences.zh: 伯克利到处都在谈论它。
它们无处不在，到处都是。

sentences.en: You were told when you had an ensemble, bring a real book.
sentences.zh: 当你参加合奏课时，老师会告诉你：带上一本《真实之书》。

sentences.en: We're going to do some tunes out of that.
sentences.zh: 我们要从那里面挑几首曲子来练。

sentences.en: But pretty quickly, Mr. Leonard discovered that the real book
sentences.zh: 但很快，伦纳德先生就发现《真实之书》

sentences.en: wasn't like the other books he needed to get for his classes.
sentences.zh: 和他上课需要的其他教材并不一样。

sentences.en: You couldn't just buy a copy in the campus bookstore.
sentences.zh: 你没法直接在校园书店里买到。

sentences.en: There was a guy who used to stand on the corner of Mass Ave near Boylston Street,
sentences.zh: 以前有个家伙常站在马萨诸塞大道靠近博伊尔斯顿街的街角，

sentences.en: and he had a box, and he would sit there, and he'd just,
sentences.zh: 他带着一个箱子，坐在那儿，然后他会说：

sentences.en: yeah, you want to buy a real book?
Want to buy a real book?
From Mr. Leonard's description, this guy basically sounded like he wandered out of a ZZ Top concert.
sentences.zh: 根据伦纳德先生的描述，这家伙听起来就像是从ZZ Top乐队的演唱会上溜出来的。

sentences.en: You know, jeans, really, really long, like, mid-back-level hair, big beard.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，穿着牛仔裤，留着非常非常长的头发，长到后背中间，还有大胡子。

sentences.en: And as I understood it, he used to get arrested about once every two weeks.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，他大约每两周就会被捕一次。

sentences.en: He would get arrested because the real book was illegal.
sentences.zh: 他会被捕是因为《真实之书》是非法的。

sentences.en: The world's most popular collection of jazz music was a totally unlicensed publication,
sentences.zh: 这本世界上最受欢迎的爵士乐曲集是一本完全未经授权的出版物，

sentences.en: a janky, self-published book created without permission from music publishers or songwriters.
sentences.zh: 一本粗制滥造、自费出版的书，在没有获得音乐出版商或词曲作者许可的情况下制作而成。

sentences.en: It was duplicated at photocopy shops and sold on street corners,
sentences.zh: 它在复印店被复制，在街角售卖，

sentences.en: out of the trunks of cars, and under the table at music stores,
sentences.zh: 从汽车后备箱里拿出来卖，或者在乐器店里私下交易，

sentences.en: where people used secret code words to make the exchange.
sentences.zh: 人们用暗号来完成这种交易。

sentences.en: The full story of how the real book came to be this bootleg bible of jazz
sentences.zh: 关于《真实之书》如何成为这本爵士乐“盗版圣经”的完整故事，

sentences.en: It's a story about what happens when an insurgent improvisational art form like jazz
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于当像爵士乐这样具有反叛性的即兴艺术形式

sentences.en: gets codified and becomes something you can learn from a book.
sentences.zh: 被编纂成册，变成你可以从书本中学习的东西时，会发生什么的故事。

sentences.en: Barry Kernfeld is a musicologist who's written a lot about the history of jazz and music piracy.
sentences.zh: 巴里·克恩菲尔德是一位音乐学家，他写过很多关于爵士乐历史和音乐盗版的文章。

sentences.en: He's also a saxophonist, and at a coffee shop gig in the 1990s,
sentences.zh: 他也是一位萨克斯手，在90年代的一次咖啡馆演出中，

sentences.en: he was opening his real book.
sentences.zh: 他打开了他的《真实之书》。

sentences.en: And I started wondering, well, we're reading all these tunes and learning to play,
sentences.zh: 我开始好奇，我们一直在读这些曲谱并学习演奏，

sentences.en: and where did the book come from?
sentences.zh: 但这本书到底是从哪儿来的呢？

sentences.en: Kernfeld says that long before the real book ever came out,
sentences.zh: 克恩菲尔德说，早在《真实之书》问世之前，

sentences.en: jazz musicians were relying on collections of music they called fake books.
sentences.zh: 爵士乐手们就依赖于他们称之为“伪书”（fake books）的乐谱集。

sentences.en: And the story of the first fake book begins in the 1940s.
sentences.zh: 而第一本“伪书”的故事始于20世纪40年代。

sentences.en: A man named George Goodwin in New York City,
sentences.zh: 纽约市有个叫乔治·古德温的人，

sentences.en: involved heavily in radio in the early 1940s,
sentences.zh: 他在40年代初深度参与广播行业，

sentences.en: was getting a little frustrated with all the intricacies of tracking, licensing.
sentences.zh: 对追踪版权和授权的繁琐细节感到有些沮丧。

sentences.en: And so he invented this thing that he called the Tune Dex.
sentences.zh: 于是他发明了一种东西，他称之为“曲调索引”（Tune Dex）。

sentences.en: The Tune Dex was an index card catalog designed for radio station employees to keep track of the songs they were playing on air.
sentences.zh: “曲调索引”是一套索引卡片目录，旨在让广播电台员工追踪他们在节目中播放的歌曲。

sentences.en: On one side, the cards had information about a particular song.
sentences.zh: 卡片的一面有关于特定歌曲的信息。

sentences.en: The composer, the publisher, the things you would need to know for paying rights.
sentences.zh: 作曲家、出版商，以及支付版权费时需要了解的内容。

sentences.en: And on the other side, they had a few lines of bite-sized sheet music,
sentences.zh: 而另一面，则有几行简化的乐谱，

sentences.en: just the song's melody, lyrics, and chords,
sentences.zh: 只有歌曲的旋律、歌词和和弦，

sentences.en: so that radio station employees could glance at it and quickly recall the song.
sentences.zh: 这样广播电台员工扫一眼就能快速回忆起这首歌。

sentences.en: But this abbreviated musical notation also made the cards useful to another group of people,
sentences.zh: 但这种简化的乐谱也让这些卡片对另一群人很有用，

sentences.en: As a black art form, jazz had developed out of a mix of other black music traditions,
sentences.zh: 作为一种黑人艺术形式，爵士乐是从多种黑人音乐传统中融合发展而来的，

sentences.en: By the 40s, a lot of jazz was popular dance music,
sentences.zh: 到了40年代，很多爵士乐成了流行的舞曲，

sentences.en: and many jazz musicians were making their money playing live gigs in small clubs and bars.
sentences.zh: 许多爵士乐手靠在小俱乐部和酒吧里现场演出赚钱。

sentences.en: The standard jazz repertoire was mostly well-known songs from Broadway
sentences.zh: 标准的爵士乐曲目大多是百老汇或

sentences.en: or New York songwriting factory Tin Pan Alley,
sentences.zh: 纽约“锡盘巷”歌曲工厂的知名歌曲，

sentences.en: like the song Night and Day by Tin Pan Alley legend Cole Porter.
sentences.zh: 比如锡盘巷传奇人物科尔·波特的《日日夜夜》（Night and Day）。

sentences.en: Jazz musicians would riff and freestyle over these songs.
sentences.zh: 爵士乐手会围绕这些歌曲进行即兴演奏和自由发挥。

sentences.en: That's always been a key part of jazz, the art of improvisation.
sentences.zh: 这一直是爵士乐的关键部分，即即兴创作的艺术。

sentences.en: But what made the average gigging trumpeter or sax player truly valuable
sentences.zh: 但让一个普通的驻场小号手或萨克斯手真正有价值的，

sentences.en: was their ability to play any one of hundreds of songs right there on the spot.
sentences.zh: 是他们能够当场演奏数百首歌曲中任何一首的能力。

sentences.en: In the 1940s, people are working steadily as musicians,
sentences.zh: 在40年代，人们作为音乐人稳定工作，

sentences.en: playing piano in nightclubs or playing in a small group in nightclubs,
sentences.zh: 在夜总会弹钢琴或在小乐队里演奏，

sentences.en: You know, the cliche of the drunken guy,
sentences.zh: 你知道那个醉汉的老梗吗，

sentences.en: hey, can you play I Left My Heart in San Francisco?
sentences.zh: “嘿，你能弹《我把心留在旧金山》吗？”

sentences.en: To be prepared for any drunken request,
sentences.zh: 为了应对任何醉酒后的点歌，

sentences.en: musicians would bring stacks and stacks of sheet music to every gig.
sentences.zh: 乐手们每次演出都会带上一大堆乐谱。

sentences.en: But lugging around a giant pile of paper was really cumbersome.
sentences.zh: 但拖着一大堆纸确实非常麻烦。

sentences.en: And that's where the Tune Decks came in.
sentences.zh: 这就是“曲调索引”派上用场的地方。

sentences.en: Someone figured out that you could gather a bunch of Tune Decks cards,
sentences.zh: 有人想出可以收集一堆“曲调索引”卡片，

sentences.en: print copies of them on sheets of paper,
add a table of contents and a simple binding,
sentences.zh: 加上目录和简单的装订，

sentences.en: and then sell the finished product directly to musicians in the form of a book.
sentences.zh: 然后以书的形式直接卖给乐手。

sentences.en: They called them fake books because they helped musicians fake their way through unfamiliar songs.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为“伪书”，因为它们帮助乐手在不熟悉的歌曲中“伪装”过关。

sentences.en: These first fake books were cheaper than regular sheet music and a lot more organized.
sentences.zh: 这些最早的伪书比普通的乐谱便宜，而且更有条理。

sentences.en: And they became an essential tool for this entire class of working musicians.
sentences.zh: 它们成了这一整类职业乐手的必备工具。

sentences.en: And then they could bring that to gigs instead of having to trawl through piles of sheet music
sentences.zh: 这样他们就可以带着书去演出，而不必在成堆的乐谱中翻找，

sentences.en: and try to keep each individual sheet in alphabetical order.
sentences.zh: 还要费力地把每一张纸按字母顺序排列。

sentences.en: You have your bound little book of 300 tunes or 500 tunes or 1,000 tunes.
sentences.zh: 你有一本装订好的小书，里面有300首、500首甚至1000首曲子。

sentences.en: And that became the first popular music fake book.
sentences.zh: 那成了第一本流行的音乐伪书。

sentences.en: Musicians loved these new fake books, but the music publishers, not so much.
sentences.zh: 乐手们很喜欢这些新伪书，但音乐出版商们就不那么高兴了。

sentences.en: They wanted musicians to buy their sheet music.
sentences.zh: 他们希望乐手购买他们的正版乐谱。

sentences.en: And so the publishing companies started cracking down on fake book bootleggers.
sentences.zh: 于是出版公司开始打击伪书盗版商。

sentences.en: The music publishers did everything they could,
sentences.zh: 音乐出版商们竭尽所能，

sentences.en: in order to suppress this new way of distributing music.
sentences.zh: 试图压制这种新的音乐传播方式。

sentences.en: But that didn't stop the bootleggers.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有阻止盗版商。

sentences.en: And by the 1950s, there were countless illegal fake books in existence,
sentences.zh: 到了50年代，市面上已经有无数非法的伪书，

sentences.en: which were being used in nightclubs all across the country.
sentences.zh: 在全国各地的夜总会里被使用。

sentences.en: But as helpful as fake books were, they had a lot of probleMs.
sentences.zh: 但尽管伪书很有用，它们也有很多问题。

sentences.en: They were notoriously illegible and confusingly laid out.
sentences.zh: 它们以字迹难以辨认和排版混乱而闻名。

sentences.en: It can't be stressed enough how deficient the old fake books were in this regard,
sentences.zh: 怎么强调旧伪书在这方面的缺陷都不为过，

sentences.en: how impossible to read, and how stupidly misrepresented they were on the page.
sentences.zh: 它们简直无法阅读，而且在页面上的呈现方式愚蠢至极。

sentences.en: Steve Swallow is a jazz musician and an all-around good guy.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫·斯沃洛是一位爵士乐手，也是个十足的好人。

sentences.en: I was like, you know, thought of as a swell guy.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，你知道，大家都认为他是个很棒的家伙。

sentences.en: I'm a bass player and I write tunes.
sentences.zh: 我是个贝斯手，我也写曲子。

sentences.en: That's the salient fact of my life.
sentences.zh: 这是我生活中最突出的事实。

sentences.en: Starting off as a young jazz musician in the 1950s,
sentences.zh: 作为一名50年代初出茅庐的年轻爵士乐手，

sentences.en: Swallow played at clubs and dances and weddings and bar mitzvahs.
sentences.zh: 斯沃洛在俱乐部、舞会、婚礼和犹太成人礼上演奏。

sentences.en: And for a lot of these gigs, he relied on these poorly designed fake books.
sentences.zh: 在很多演出中，他都依赖这些设计糟糕的伪书。

sentences.en: Working on jazz music seriously, one of the first things I did was to buy a fake book.
sentences.zh: 认真从事爵士乐工作时，我做的第一件事就是买了一本伪书。

sentences.en: And they were just vexing and badly, badly written.
sentences.zh: 它们简直让人恼火，而且写得非常、非常糟糕。

sentences.en: The other big problem with these fake books at this point was that the music inside felt really out of date.
sentences.zh: 当时这些伪书的另一个大问题是，里面的音乐感觉非常过时。

sentences.en: The fake books hadn't changed since the mid-40s, but jazz had.
sentences.zh: 伪书自40年代中期以来就没变过，但爵士乐已经变了。

sentences.en: Disillusioned by commercial jazz that appealed to mainstream white audiences,
sentences.zh: 由于对迎合主流白人听众的商业爵士乐感到幻灭，

sentences.en: a new generation of black musicians took jazz improvisation to a new level,
sentences.zh: 新一代黑人音乐家将爵士即兴演奏提升到了一个新的水平，

sentences.en: experimenting with more angular harmonies, technically demanding melodies, and blindingly fast tempos.
sentences.zh: 尝试更尖锐的和声、技术要求极高的旋律，以及快得惊人的节奏。

sentences.en: Their new style was called bebop.
sentences.zh: 他们的新风格被称为“比波普”（bebop）。

sentences.en: That was bebop legend Charlie Parker.
sentences.zh: 那是比波普传奇查理·帕克。

sentences.en: And bebop was just the beginning.
sentences.zh: 而比波普仅仅是个开始。

sentences.en: Then came hard bop and modal jazz, spearheaded by Miles Davis.
sentences.zh: 接着是迈尔斯·戴维斯领衔的硬波普和调式爵士。

sentences.en: Then you had the wild, dissonant free jazz of people like Ornette Coleman.
sentences.zh: 然后是奥内特·科尔曼等人狂野、不和谐的自由爵士。

sentences.en: And the electrified jazz fusion of Herbie Hancock.
sentences.zh: 还有赫比·汉考克的电声爵士融合乐。

sentences.en: By the 1970s, jazz had exploded into this constellation of different styles.
sentences.zh: 到了70年代，爵士乐已经爆炸式地发展成各种风格的集合体。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the economics of jazz had shifted too.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，爵士乐的经济状况也发生了变化。

sentences.en: There were fewer clubs and smaller paychecks.
sentences.zh: 俱乐部变少了，报酬也变少了。

sentences.en: University jazz programs also started popping up around this time,
sentences.zh: 大学爵士乐课程也大约在此时开始兴起，

sentences.en: providing steady teaching gigs to established musicians.
sentences.zh: 为资深音乐人提供了稳定的教学工作。

sentences.en: And increasingly, the ivory tower became a place for young musicians to learn.
sentences.zh: 而且，“象牙塔”越来越多地成为年轻音乐人学习的地方。

sentences.en: And if you're going to jazz school, you need jazz books.
sentences.zh: 如果你要上爵士乐学校，你就需要爵士乐教材。

sentences.en: But the fake books at the time hadn't kept up with the music.
sentences.zh: 但当时的伪书并没有跟上音乐的发展。

sentences.en: They still contained the same old-fashioned collection of standards,
sentences.zh: 它们仍然包含着同样老派的标准曲合集，

sentences.en: with the same old-fashioned collection of chord changes.
sentences.zh: 以及同样老派的和弦进行。

sentences.en: So if a young jazz musician wanted to try and play like Charles Mingus or Sonny Rollins,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果一个年轻的爵士乐手想尝试演奏像查尔斯·明格斯或桑尼·罗林斯那样的音乐，

sentences.en: they weren't going to learn from a book.
sentences.zh: 他们是没法从书本上学到的。

sentences.en: That is, until two college kids invented the real book.
sentences.zh: 直到两个大学生发明了《真实之书》。

sentences.en: I don't want to overemphasize my role in it, which was minor.
sentences.zh: 我不想过分强调我在其中的作用，那很小。

sentences.en: In the mid-70s, Steve Swallow began teaching at Boston's Berklee College of Music,
sentences.zh: 70年代中期，史蒂夫·斯沃洛开始在波士顿的伯克利音乐学院任教，

sentences.en: an elite private music school that boasted one of the first jazz performance programs in the country.
sentences.zh: 这是一所精英私立音乐学校，拥有全国首批爵士乐表演课程之一。

sentences.en: Swallow had only been teaching at Berklee for a few months,
sentences.zh: 斯沃洛在伯克利教书才几个月，

sentences.en: when two students approached him about a secret project.
sentences.zh: 就有两个学生找他谈一个秘密项目。

sentences.en: I keep referring to them as the two guys who wrote the book,
sentences.zh: 我一直称他们为“写书的那两个人”，

sentences.en: because way back when, they swore me to secrecy.
sentences.zh: 因为很久以前，他们让我发誓保密。

sentences.en: They made me agree that I would not divulge their names.
sentences.zh: 他们让我答应不泄露他们的名字。

sentences.en: The two guys wanted to make a new fake book,
sentences.zh: 那两个家伙想做一本新的伪书，

sentences.en: one that actually catered to the needs of contemporary jazz musicians
sentences.zh: 一本真正能满足当代爵士乐手需求，

sentences.en: and reflected the current state of jazz.
sentences.zh: 并反映爵士乐现状的书。
他们需要史蒂夫的帮助。
这就是他们的推销方式。

sentences.en: They pitched it that they wanted to write a fake book
that would actually be useful to an 18-year-old person
who wanted to become a jazz musician.
sentences.zh: 想成为爵士乐手的人有用的书。

sentences.en: As a longtime user of some pretty horrible fake books,
sentences.zh: 作为一些相当糟糕的伪书的长期用户，

sentences.en: He thought that a modern, well-made jazz fake book
sentences.zh: 他认为一本现代、制作精良的爵士伪书，

sentences.en: would be an essential improvement for his students.
